assertion: Chief O'Connor utilized Griffin as the primary underworld contact to vet arriving outlaws and manage layover tribute.
qualifications: Documented by Minnesota Historical Society syntheses; no signed correspondence between them exists.

assertion: Following Griffin's death in 1913, Dan Hogan succeeded him as chief intermediary and underworld liaison.
Hogan operated the Green Lantern as the central nexus connecting underworld fugitives with municipal police leadership.
qualifications: Historical accounts describe operational accommodation; individual transactions were unrecorded.

assertion: Gleckman influenced juror Fuchs during the 1934 tax trial through cash payment promises and coerced loan approvals.
qualifications: Formally established by federal court findings in 1938 criminal contempt proceedings.

assertion: Sawyer designated Bremer as an extortion target for the Barker-Karpis gang in preference to robbing a bank.
qualifications: Attributed to post-arrest investigative reconstructions in FBI summary reports.

assertion: Magee served as the coerced courier and intermediary between Bremer's captors and the family.
qualifications: Documented in federal case records; actions performed under severe duress.

assertion: Frechette accompanied Dillinger as his companion, sharing refuge at the Lincoln Court apartments under an alias.
qualifications: Documented in federal harboring indictment and trial records.
